The only protection is a 100-request bucket keyed by the caller-supplied/proxy-derived identity. Rotating `X-Forwarded-For` values can create new buckets and bypass the intended per-client limit.

title: Development error handler is enabled on the application server
description: The application unconditionally installs the `errorhandler` development middleware after all routes. Errors reaching this middleware can produce verbose HTML responses containing stack traces, source locations, and internal implementation details. No environment check or production-safe error handler is present in this file, so an attacker can trigger errors on public endpoints and obtain diagnostic information useful for further attacks.

title: Hardcoded weak cookie-signing secret
description: The server uses the hardcoded string `kekse` as the cookie-parser signing secret. Any signed cookie used by the application is protected by a source-controlled, predictable secret rather than a deployment-specific high-entropy secret. An attacker who obtains or guesses this value can forge signed cookies, potentially bypassing any security decision based on them. This is also a dangerous hardcoded authentication/cryptographic secret.

title: Log directory listing is reachable before its access-control middleware
description: The application exposes a directory index for `/support/logs` before installing the access-control middleware for that path. A request to the directory itself is handled by `serveIndex` at line 280, so the later `verify.accessControlChallenges()` middleware does not protect the listing. This can disclose log filenames, timestamps, and other operational metadata even though individual log-file serving is registered afterward.

title: Textbook RSA encryption makes the confidential document directly recoverable
description: The script uses textbook RSA to encrypt each character independently with a public exponent and modulus. Because each plaintext character has a very small domain (typically at most 256 common ASCII/extended-ASCII values), an attacker who obtains `announcement_encrypted.md` can compute `pow(candidate, e, N)` for every candidate character and build a direct ciphertext-to-character mapping. The deterministic per-character encryption also exposes repeated-character patterns and provides no semantic security. Consequently, the supposedly confidential document can be recovered without the private key.

The plaintext is processed one character at a time, ensuring each character is encrypted independently rather than using a randomized, semantically secure encryption scheme.

Each character's small integer code point is passed directly to textbook RSA using the public exponent and modulus and written as a standalone ciphertext value. There is no padding, randomness, authenticated encryption, or batching, so ciphertext values can be matched against all candidate character values.

title: Unbounded privileged token minting permits unlimited supply inflation
description: The contract exposes an owner-authorized minting function with no maximum supply, per-account limit, or other monetary policy constraint. The constructor creates an initial supply, but the owner can subsequently call `mintTokens` with an arbitrary amount and increase both `_totalSupply` and the recipient balance indefinitely. If BEE is intended to represent a fixed or bounded supply, a compromised owner key—or an owner acting maliciously—can create unlimited tokens, dilute holders, and manipulate the token economy. The `onlyOwner` check prevents ordinary unauthenticated callers from invoking the function, so this is an insecure economic design rather than a direct authorization bypass.

The function only checks that the caller is the contract owner; it imposes no cap on `amount`, no maximum total supply, and no issuance schedule.
The arbitrary amount is passed to `_mint`, which increases `_totalSupply` and the recipient's balance without any upper bound, creating new tokens.
